Laura/Team — I pulled the trace and the token-level telemetry. Preliminary findings:

1) The incident correlates with a burst window mis-synchronization between MediGenix tenant quotas and the global guardrail. MediGenix has an allowed burst credit bucket that refills on a different cadence than the global per-region safety valve; when their active traffic pattern spiked we observed a rapid depletion of tenant burst credits followed by the global guardrail stepping in and returning 429s.

2) Concurrently, KV cache warmup for long-context sessions produced transient CPU pressure on the shard serving that tenant which exaggerated tail latency (those calls are CPU-bound and got queued behind non-KV requests).

Immediate mitigations I can apply (minutes):
- Temporarily raise MediGenix tenant burst bucket by 2.5x for the next 4 hours to give breathing room.
- Move their production traffic to a less-loaded slab (manual routing) for the immediate window.

Longer-term fixes (days):
- Align refill cadence between tenant buckets and the global safety valve; add clock-sync monotonic check to the quota calculator.
- Add a fast-path for KV cache warmups to avoid CPU queuing during traffic surges.

I recommend we do the temporary burst increase now and monitor. Priya — I’ll need authorization to change the tenant config (this is a conservative temporary bump).

Karthik Iyer
Staff Platform SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident update: root cause and next steps (INF-5421)

Team / Laura — final update from engineering after the deeper investigation:

Root cause summary: a mismatch in the burst refill cadence and a missed monotonic check allowed tenant credits to be consumed quicker than anticipated; the global safety valve logic assumed a longer refill window and triggered request shedding. Secondary factor was KV cache busy-waiting during long-context warmups which amplified tail latency.

What we changed (rolled out 09 Oct 17:00 PT):
- Aligned refill cadence across tenant buckets and the global guardrail (config change + unit tests).
- Added a monotonic timestamp check to the quota calculator to prevent backward-time refills.
- Introduced a fast-path CPU reservation for KV cache warmups to prevent queueing under load.
- Created an operational runbook for similar incidents and a dashboard tile showing tenant burst exhaustion before global shed.

Customer impact and remediation:
- MediGenix saw a drop in error rate from 12% -> 0.4% after the temporary bump; the permanent config fix removes the timing mismatch so steady-state risk is mitigated.
- We will propose a goodwill credit for the affected window as part of RG-8342 negotiations; Priya will draft language with Neha and Procurement.

Open items:
- Post-incident review doc (INF-5421) will be published by Monday.
- Marissa: board-facing one-paragraph summary (I included a suggested blurb in the doc).

Karthik
Staff Platform SRE, Redwood Inference
